content.text:
**Choose Sentry**, unless your product is mostly mobile, in which case consider Bugsnag. This comes from my background knowledge, not a live check. Pricing and plan limits change often, so confirm them on each vendor's pricing page before you commit.

| | **Sentry** | **Rollbar** | **Bugsnag** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Core strength** | Errors plus tracing, performance and session replay in one tool | Fast error grouping, deploy tracking, a simple workflow | Mobile stability scores and release health |
| **SDK coverage** | Broadest (100+ platforms, strong web, backend and mobile) | Good backend and web coverage | Strong mobile (iOS, Android, React Native, Unity), good web |
| **Pricing model** | Usage-based. Free tier, then a Team plan at roughly $25–30/month, with unlimited users | Event-based, with a free tier and low-cost entry plans. Members are generally unlimited | Event-based and typically pricier at similar volume. Tied to the SmartBear suite |
| **Self-hosting** | Yes (open core), but it takes real ops effort | No | No |
| **Ecosystem** | Largest community, many integrations (GitHub, Slack, Jira, Linear), heavily documented | Solid integrations, smaller community | Solid integrations, smaller community |
| **Weak spots** | Quota and overage management takes attention. The UI can feel busy | Fewer features beyond errors. Less momentum | Less compelling for web-only teams. Fewer extras |

**Why Sentry for a 10-person team**
- **Cost:** Unlimited users on paid plans means no per-seat cost as you grow.
- **Consolidation:** Tracing and replay can replace one or two other tools later, so you don't have to add them separately.
- **Hiring:** More engineers have used Sentry, and finding answers is easier.
- **Lock-in:** You can self-host if cost or data residency becomes an issue.

**When to pick something else**
- **Bugsnag:** Your product is primarily a mobile app and you care about crash-free sessions and release stability as a headline metric.
- **Rollbar:** You want something small and simple, you only need error tracking, and you like its deploy-correlation workflow.

**Practical tips**
- Set spend caps and rate limits on day one. This is the main way Sentry bills surprise teams.
- Run a one-week trial in a real service before deciding. All three have free tiers, and SDK setup takes under an hour each.

If you tell me your stack (web, mobile, backend languages) and your expected monthly error volume, I can narrow this down. I can also look up current pricing if you'd like.
